EDITORIAL
This autumn and winter, Narbo Via invites you to share a cultural season that brings the museum's five-year anniversary festivities to a close. Throughout the months, the Archaeology Meetings of the Narbonnaise, the Balèti with the Théâtre+Cinéma, the musical procession Migrare with the Patio des Arts, and the Night of Reading with the MJC invite us to bring together knowledge, memories and cultures.
The contemporary art trail The Breath of Time accompanies the end of the celebrations like a true common thread.
By bringing civilisations and imaginaries into dialogue, the artist Jiang Qiong Er invites us to reflect on an essential question: how do we form a society with our specific and shared cultures and histories? This reflection echoes the ambition Narbo Via has carried since its opening: to make the museum a place where the diversity of stories, cultures and perspectives unfolds around a common heritage, where knowledge meets in order to better understand the past and shed light on the present.
The exhibition Lagoon Memories, built around a participatory collection, is an opportunity to stage these memories with the show by the Anapnoi company, in which storytelling theatre, music and images give a voice to the women and men who shape our region.
The lectures, tours, accessible events, creative workshops and activities offered to families every weekend and during school holidays are all opportunities to come together. This ever more inclusive approach has been recognised by two national awards: the Mom'Art trophy, which rewards initiatives aimed at families, and the 2026 Accessible Tourism Trophy.
As the festivities of this fifth anniversary come to an end, I would like to thank all those who, since the museum opened, have helped bring this place to life: loyal or passing visitors, partners, artists, researchers, associations and teams. It is with you that Narbo Via continues its story and affirms its vocation as a museum open to its region, where heritage only makes sense when it is shared and lived together.
I look forward to seeing you for the final highlights of this lovely anniversary and wish you a wonderful season at Narbo Via.
Carole Delga
President of the Occitanie / Pyrénées-Méditerranée Region
Chair of the board of directors of the EPCC Narbo Via

1 MUSEUM, 2 SITES
The public cultural cooperation establishment (EPCC) Narbo Via brings together three sites devoted to the Roman history of Narbonne
The Narbo Via museum, designed by the architectural firm Foster+Partners, brings the Roman city of Narbo Martius back to life. Through more than 1,300 exhibited pieces, the capital of the province of Gallia Narbonensis reveals its treasures: a collection of 760 funerary blocks, mosaics and wall paintings worthy of Pompeii, and 3D reconstructions of the ancient city and its port.
The Horreum, in the heart of the modern city, consists of underground galleries built in the 1st century BC. They were meant to form the foundations of a building, probably a market or a warehouse, whose secrets research has not yet fully uncovered…
Amphoralis, in Sallèles-d'Aude, presents the remains of an ancient workshop producing Gallic amphorae and building materials. The museum overlooks the archaeological excavations, while an outdoor trail leads to reconstructions of the potters' village in a preserved environment.
7:
NARBO VIA NEWS
The restoration of the archaeological artefacts discovered in the necropolis of the Berges de la Robine
Between 2017 and 2020, Inrap archaeologists carried out an exceptionally large excavation on a plot next to the museum to explore a large necropolis of the Roman city. Exceptional is indeed the word that describes this site: because of the area explored, more than 2,000 m², which made it possible to study for the first time in Narbonne such an extensive funerary area and to understand its organisation and evolution; but also because of the excellent preservation of the remains, revealing numerous traces of funerary practices and rituals rarely observable.
By common agreement between all the partners (State, Region, Grand Narbonne conurbation, City of Narbonne, developer), the artefacts discovered during the excavation were assigned to the EPCC Narbo Via for their conservation and presentation to the general public. The EPCC has thus begun to receive the archaeological artefacts in its storerooms and is preparing a major temporary exhibition planned for 2027 in partnership with Inrap. To ensure good conservation of these artefacts and an optimal presentation to the public, a restoration project has been launched: nearly 255 objects will receive treatment, from simple surface cleaning to fundamental restoration allowing an object broken into several pieces to be reassembled. This phase will also be an opportunity to better understand these objects in their materiality, such as the stele decorated with bust portraits, which is partly covered by a mysterious black crust: its restoration will make it possible to identify the nature of this crust and perhaps to better understand the history of the object.
Archaeological excavations of a necropolis at the Berges de la Robine – 23 October 2020

CONTEMPORARY ART TRAIL
JIANG QIONG ER –
THE BREATH OF TIME
In the heart of its permanent collections, Narbo Via presents until 3 January an exceptional exhibition by the French-Chinese contemporary artist Jiang Qiong Er. Inspired by China's thousand-year-old artistic traditions, which she reinterprets in a resolutely contemporary approach, the artist presents a body of works that raise the question of living together. Mythical creatures, paintings in natural pigments inspired by decorated caves, works on wax canvas and creations around the Nüshu script link civilisations, mythological imaginaries and the different layers of time.
In resonance with the Narbo Via collections, this exhibition invites a renewed look at the museum.
Exhibition curators: Jiang Qiong Er, in dialogue with the Narbo Via team. Included in the admission ticket: 40 works to discover along the exhibition trail in the museum's permanent collection.

THE TEMPORARY EXHIBITION,
LAGOON MEMORIES
Born from a participatory photographic collection organised by Narbo Via between February and June 2025, echoing the exhibition Stopover in the Roman Mediterranean, the ancient ports of Narbonne, this exhibition, in partnership with the Departmental Archives of the Aude and the Narbonnaise en Méditerranée Regional Nature Park, presents a selection of photographs and testimonies from a set of more than 650 images collected across the lagoon area. Combining photographs, creations, and archaeological and ethnographic objects, the trail is organised around five themes that illustrate the many uses of this territory: developing, making, sailing, exploiting and studying. Hands-on activities, workshops and participatory spaces invite visitors to contribute to this collective memory and to discover the former territory of the ancient ports in a new way.
Exhibition curators: Narbo Via team. Narbo Via Museum. Included in the museum admission ticket.
Do you also have photos and stories to share?
The collection is still open at the Departmental Archives!
To take part, contact the Departmental Archives directly by email at archives@aude.fr or by phone on 04.68.11.31.54.

€12 / €7 for beneficiaries of free admission to the museum, duo 1 adult + 1 child: €15 (+ €4 per additional child). Adults and children from 9 years old. Booking recommended (8 people maximum)
In 27 BC, the emperor Augustus, adopted son of the great and glorious Caesar, travels to Narbonne. But the period is troubled: some merchants and soldiers from his close guard are plotting and want to assassinate him, like Caesar in Rome 17 years earlier… Just as you are about to receive an honorary title from the emperor in person, you are taken prisoner in the underground passages of the Horreum and realise that Augustus is in great danger. Only one solution: escape and warn him as soon as possible. To do so, you will have to take on the challenges of the Horreum, but will you make it in time?

The lectures offered at the Narbo Via museum on certain Thursday evenings are divided into several series:

Wine faces many challenges and consumption habits are changing, requiring winegrowers to adapt. Light, simple, sociable yet delicious and surprising wines are thus joining the aperitif. Come and discover how these new wines are made and chosen.
Nadine Franjus, journalist and oenologist, explores the evolution of the wine world. The presentation will be followed by a book sale and signing of her book In vino apéro.

Thursday 15/10 at 6 pm
"Exhibition" series

Together, they will discuss the dialogue between cultures, artistic exchanges between East and West, and how works of art travel through time while nourishing contemporary creation. 33:
Study day: The contribution of preventive archaeology to knowledge of the urban topography of ancient Narbonne
Thursday 22/10 from 9 am to 6 pm
"Silence, we're digging" series
At the Museum – auditorium. Free. Booking recommended
For almost 40 years, preventive archaeology has accompanied the development of the city of Narbonne, in the form of interventions prior to the construction of new facilities. To date, nearly 330 surveys and excavations have been prescribed within the municipal area, for a cumulative surface of nearly 370 hectares.
If we stop at the gates of the necropolises to consider only the city as it can be reconstructed at the end of the 1st century AD, the data now available provide the expected perspective to feed initial syntheses on the morphology of a capital city whose area reached, at that date, nearly one hundred hectares. This is what this study day, organised by the laboratory Archéologie des Sociétés Méditerranéennes, proposes.
Oil and profit! An imperial villa and its estate in Croatia
Thursday 19/11 at 6 pm
"Silence, we're digging" series
At the Museum – auditorium. €5 / Free for under-18s and people on minimum social benefits. Booking recommended
Corinne Rousse has been excavating the site of Loron – Santa Marina, located in Istria (Croatia), for more than ten years. It is a maritime villa with a large oil press including mills and presses. These installations, common in Istrian villas, stand out here for their dimensions, with no known equivalent in the Roman world. The archaeologist will present the results of the research carried out with her team, in particular on the owners of this extraordinary villa.
Corinne Rousse is an archaeologist and researcher at Aix-Marseille University. She works on Roman Antiquity, in particular on villas and rural settlement in the north-Adriatic Mediterranean, through the study of architecture, domestic spaces and the economic dynamics of provincial societies.

What was the place of people with disabilities in Antiquity? Archaeological discoveries shed light on the daily life, status and care of people with different or sick bodies. A lecture that invites a new look at disability in ancient societies and feeds reflection on inclusion today.
Valérie Delattre is an archaeo-anthropologist at Inrap, a specialist in funerary practices. She studies disabling pathologies, care and support for "different bodies" in past societies. Lecture organised in partnership with Inrap.
New research on the House with Porticoes at Clos de la Lombarde

A renewed study, a fresh look at the metamorphoses of this residence bearing witness to the daily life of the colony of Narbo Martius.
Clara Prats, doctor in archaeology, is a specialist in Roman painting, and Arnaud Davoisne is a member of the Friends of Clos de la Lombarde.

NON-SCHOOL GROUPS
Groups of 10 people or more are welcomed by compulsory reservation, for a visit of their choice: a discovery trail presenting the essentials of the Museum, the Horreum and Amphoralis sites or the temporary exhibitions; an "archeonomad" visit from one site to another; themed tours to explore the backstage or the architecture of the Museum or to awaken the senses in the Amphoralis garden; or playful and offbeat tours to explore the collections with a different eye. Details of the offer are available on request and can also be downloaded from our website narbovia.fr.
